system.name: RE-Bench
system.one_liner: A benchmark of seven ML research-engineering environments where human experts and AI agents work under the same conditions and are scored the same way.

content.variant_note: one environment drawn in the abstract: resources copied to the agent's machine, the agent submits, a scoring function answers, with three numbered narration callouts at the sides
content.argues: Humans and AI agents are put into the same scored environment: same resources, same machine, and feedback from the scoring function at any time.
content.subject: The structure of one RE-Bench environment: resources, agent environment, scoring loop and score records.

evidence: RE-Bench is a collection of seven hand-crafted environments intended to test the AI R&D capabilities of current AI systems.
Humans and AI agents are tested under the same conditions.
given a starting solution, access to a machine with 1–6 H100 GPUs, and a way to score their progress

summary: RE-Bench is a benchmark of seven hand-crafted ML research-engineering environments in which human experts and AI agents are tested under the same conditions. Figure 1 shows one environment in the abstract. A pink Environment Resources box holds the instructions, datasets, starting solution and a scoring function; a copy is passed to a blue Agent Environment with an H100 GPU, network access and the files, where a person or a robot agent works on the task. The agent's submission (trained_model/) goes up to the scoring function, which sends back a scorer message and writes score records. Three numbered cream callouts at the sides narrate setting up, starting (SSH + VSCode for humans, scaffolding code for AI agents) and acting.
